name: Cornmeal Drop Biscuits with Pork Sausage Gravy & Butter Lettuce-Radish Salad (Two Ways)

instructions.primary_message: This recipe was created to feed two adults and two young children. You know your child (their tastes and appetite) best. Use this recipe as a template, adjusting ingredients, cooking methods, and portions as needed.
In a medium bowl, combine flour, cornmeal, baking powder, sugar, and salt, then stir to combine the dry ingredients.
instructions.secondary_message:
¾ cup all-purpose flour
¼ cup polenta (cornmeal)
1 tsp baking powder
½ tsp brown sugar
¼ tsp salt

instructions.primary_message: Using a box grater, coarsely grate cold butter into the bowl with the dry ingredients. Using two hands, combine the flour and butter by rubbing the mixture between your thumbs and fingers until it looks crumbly. Add milk and stir to combine the biscuit dough.

Using a scant ¼-cup measure, drop portions of the dough onto a baking sheet pan, spacing them 2-inches apart (you should have 6 biscuits in total). Place in the preheated oven and bake until biscuits are lightly golden, about 15 minutes. Remove from oven.
Meanwhile, preheat a large skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, slice sausages crosswise into ½-inch thick rounds.

Once the skillet is hot, add butter and swirl to coat the bottom; add sausage and cook, stirring occasionally, until golden brown and crispy, 5-6 minutes. Transfer to a plate and set aside. (Reserve skillet with drippings for later use.)
Meanwhile, wash and dry the fresh produce.
instructions.secondary_message:
½ bunch radish
½ small pkg chives
½ head butter (Boston) lettuce
1 Gala apple

instructions.primary_message: Place oil, vinegar, Dijon, honey, and spices in a clean medium bowl, then whisk to combine the dressing.
instructions.secondary_message:
2 tsp extra virgin olive oil
2 tsp white wine vinegar
½ tsp Dijon mustard
½ tsp honey
¼ tsp garlic powder
¼ tsp salt
⅛ tsp black pepper

instructions.primary_message: Using a clean cutting board, trim and slice radishes crosswise into thin rounds. Add to the bowl with the dressing.
Chop chives into small pieces. Add half to the bowl and set aside. (Reserve remaining chives for serving.)
Return skillet (with drippings) to medium-high heat, add broth, butter, and spices, then stir to combine. Bring to a simmer.
instructions.secondary_message:
2 cups chicken or vegetable broth
butter, unsalted
½ tsp Italian seasoning
⅛ tsp salt
⅛ tsp black pepper

instructions.primary_message: Meanwhile, in a small bowl, make a slurry by whisking water with flour until smooth. Add slurry to the skillet and stir to combine. Return sausage to the skillet, stir once more to combine, cover, and reduce heat to low. Cook, stirring occasionally, until gravy has thickened, 5-6 minutes. Remove from heat.
While the gravy is cooking, chop or tear lettuce into bite-sized pieces. Add to the bowl with the dressing, toss to combine the salad, and set aside.
Quarter, core, and slice apple into wedges. Split two biscuits in half and spread with butter.

FOR THE KID PLATES: Divide apple wedges, buttered biscuits, and 1 cup of sausage gravy between plates. 

FOR THE ADULT PLATES: Divide remaining biscuits and salad between plates. Top biscuits with remaining sausage gravy, then sprinkle with reserved chives. Enjoy!
